task: Overhaul the Hermes product cover and portfolio visualization system across FrankX, GenCreator, Starlight Intelligence, and Arcanea.
surface: 1080x1440 product covers, 1200x630 open graph crops, and 1920x1080 portfolio overview
audience: Founder-operators, AI-native creators, sovereign-system builders, and worldbuilders evaluating distinct product offers.
first_read: The covers are legible, but founder review found that the four brands still read as variants of one dark technical house style.

references.label: Audited Hermes baseline
references.reason: Defines the failure modes that the new system must remove.

references.label: Canonical product slate
references.reason: Supplies product names, types, status, and URLs without inventing market truth.

references.label: Canonical identity assets
references.source: FrankX, GenCreator, and Arcanea production-repo public brand folders

references.label: SIS sovereignty proof source
references.reason: Reuses an inspected, locally owned premium proof visual.

references.label: Founder visual review
references.reason: Supersedes the maker self-score and records the foundation-level rejection.

keep: the complete 47-item inventory as information, not as an approved visual system
avoid: one sparse template across unrelated product forms
generated public text or fake UI
launch theater for validation or internal products
status pills and mono readouts as marketing chrome
treating canonical logos and fonts as approved by default
direction.signature: Rejected. Product mechanisms were made visible, but the shared rendering grammar overwhelmed the intended brand distinctions.
system: canonical identity assets copied from production repos
bundled local fonts with no remote dependency

asset_quality.why_premium: The semantic layer is exact and editable, but technical correctness did not produce an approved identity or premium brand result.

artifacts.notes: Canonical cropped wordmark, clean title, evidence signal, decision gate, and deliverables checked at 1080×1440.
Canonical wordmark and mark, exact owned-work loop diagram, legible hierarchy, and no fake UI.
No invented logo; local proof asset, title, validation status, and four kit actions inspected.
Generated codex source, canonical wordmark, product/world rail distinction, title, and mechanism inspected.
All cover examples display intact; manifest-derived 14/23/10 release-state counts and labels are legible.
All 47 supplied product names, forms, source statuses, brands, and public/validation/internal classifications are visible in one deterministic inventory.
All four 1200×630 exports were visually inspected for crop, title wrapping, accent, and thumbnail legibility.

checks.name: asset-tier
checks.evidence: Tier C deterministic masters are the correct primary medium; Arcanea adds a Tier B generated source and SIS reuses owned Tier A/B proof media.

checks.name: canonical-identity
checks.evidence: FrankX, GenCreator, and Arcanea use production-repo assets. SIS records the absence of a verified logo and does not invent one.

checks.name: product-form-fit
checks.evidence: Sprint, pack, kit, and world-context kit use distinct mechanisms and compositions.

checks.name: export-inspection
checks.evidence: Four portrait covers, four OG crops, the hero overview, and the complete 47-product matrix were inspected from actual PNG exports.

checks.name: visual-qa
checks.evidence: No clipped titles, fake UI, generated public copy, missing logo assets, or unreadable primary hierarchy found.

checks.name: founder-taste-review
checks.evidence: Founder rejected the complete visual foundation and requested a ground-up rethink of logos, fonts, capitalization, taste, and brand separation.

checks.name: cross-brand-distinctiveness
checks.evidence: Dark fields, technical annotations, panel systems, glow accents, and system diagrams recur across all four brands.

checks.name: capitalization-preference
checks.evidence: The renderer hard-codes uppercase eyebrows, statuses, brand labels, and metadata despite the founder's preference against all caps.

checks.name: truth-and-release-state
checks.evidence: All four products are labeled Validation concept; no price, customer, availability, or deployment claim was added.

score.notes: The original maker self-score of 29/30 is invalidated. The post-review diagnostic keeps credit for legibility, accuracy, provenance, and editable production, but fails brand distinctiveness, typography preference, authorship, and usefulness as an identity system.

known_risks: None of the four benchmark covers or overview visuals is approved for publication or reuse as a style reference.
FrankX, GenCreator, and Arcanea logos and type choices need comparative reassessment; SIS needs a wordmark-first identity decision.
The 47-item inventory data may be reused, but only after each brand has an approved visual territory.
Automated quality checks remain capable of false-positive approval until human-first gates are propagated to canonical design standards.
